questions.skill_name: Identify security controls and explain how they mitigate risks
questions.stem: Which of the following is a technique used to segment a network?

choices.text: Installing antivirus software on all endpoint devices
Enabling HTTPS on an organization's public-facing web server
Creating VLANs to separate groups of devices into distinct logical segments
Requiring multi-factor authentication for all user logins

questions.explanation:
VLANs (Virtual Local Area Networks) are a core network segmentation technique that
      logically separate groups of devices even when they share the same physical switching
      infrastructure. Devices in different VLANs cannot communicate directly without passing
      through a Layer 3 routing device. The other options are legitimate security controls
      but operate at different layers, endpoint protection, transport-layer encryption, and
      access authentication, none of which create network-level boundaries between device groups.

distractor_rationale.A:
Antivirus software is an endpoint control that protects individual devices after a
        threat has reached them. It does not establish any boundary between network segments.
distractor_rationale.B:
HTTPS encrypts data in transit between a client and server but does not isolate network
        segments from each other. All devices on a flat network remain reachable regardless of
        whether HTTPS is in use.
distractor_rationale.D:
MFA is an identity and authentication control. It can restrict who accesses a resource
        but does not create network-layer separation between device groups.

questions.skill_name: Identify security controls and explain how they mitigate risks
questions.stem:
A network administrator configures separate VLANs for the HR department and the
      Engineering department on the same physical switch. What does this configuration
      primarily accomplish?

choices.text: It encrypts all traffic traveling between HR and Engineering devices.
It separates the two departments into distinct logical network segments.
It prevents external attackers from reaching either department's devices.
It automatically applies firewall rules to traffic between the two departments.

questions.explanation:
VLANs create logical network segments on shared physical infrastructure. Devices assigned
      to different VLANs cannot communicate directly with each other, traffic must pass through
      a Layer 3 device (a router or Layer 3 switch) where access controls can be enforced. This
      separates the HR and Engineering broadcast domains even though both departments share the
      same physical switch hardware.

distractor_rationale.A:
VLANs do not encrypt traffic. Encryption is a separate control applied at the transport
        (TLS) or application layer, independent of how the network is segmented.
distractor_rationale.C:
VLANs control internal traffic flow between segments. Protection against external
        attackers is handled by a separate perimeter control such as a firewall or edge router.
distractor_rationale.D:
VLAN assignment by itself does not configure firewall rules. Firewall ACLs must be
        explicitly created on the routing device that handles inter-VLAN traffic.

questions.skill_name: Identify security controls and explain how they mitigate risks
questions.stem: Which of the following best describes a security benefit of network segmentation?

choices.text: It eliminates the need for encryption because traffic stays within isolated segments.
It improves network performance by reducing the number of nodes in each broadcast domain.
It limits the spread of an attack by containing compromised devices within a single segment.
It prevents insider threats by blocking all employee access to sensitive servers.

questions.explanation:
Network segmentation limits lateral movement. If an attacker compromises one device, they
      are contained within that device's segment and cannot directly reach devices in other
      segments. The attacker must traverse a controlled inter-segment routing point, where
      ACLs or firewall rules can detect and block the traversal attempt, before reaching
      resources in a different segment. Containing the blast radius of a compromise is the
      primary security rationale for segmentation.

distractor_rationale.A:
Segmentation does not replace encryption. Data can still be intercepted by other devices
        within the same segment, and traffic traversing inter-VLAN routing points is also
        exposed without separate encryption controls.
distractor_rationale.B:
Smaller broadcast domains do improve network performance (fewer unnecessary broadcast
        packets), but this is an operational benefit, not a security one. Students should
        distinguish performance improvements from security controls.
distractor_rationale.D:
Segmentation controls the flow of traffic between network zones, it does not block
        all employee access to sensitive servers. Doing so would prevent legitimate access
        and defeat the operational purpose of the servers.

questions.skill_name: Identify security controls and explain how they mitigate risks
questions.stem:
A hospital network is segmented into three VLANs: one for patient monitoring devices,
      one for administrative workstations, and one for the billing system. An attacker
      successfully installs malware on an administrative workstation. Which outcome is most
      likely as a direct consequence of the segmentation?

choices.text: The attacker cannot reach patient monitoring devices or the billing system without traversing an inter-VLAN routing control point.
The malware will be automatically detected and removed by the VLAN switch firmware.
The malware will be confined to the workstation's hard drive with no network access at all.
The attacker will gain access to all three VLANs because malware can forge VLAN tags.

questions.explanation:
VLAN segmentation prevents direct Layer 2 communication between segments. To move from
      the administrative VLAN to the patient monitoring or billing VLANs, traffic must be
      routed through a Layer 3 device where ACLs or firewall rules can inspect and block it.
      The segmentation does not eliminate the threat, the admin workstation is still
      compromised, but it forces the attacker through a chokepoint, disrupting lateral
      movement and buying defenders time to detect and respond.

distractor_rationale.B:
Switches enforce VLAN membership based on port assignment or 802.1Q tags. They do not
        perform malware scanning. Malware detection is an endpoint or IDS/IPS function,
        separate from switching infrastructure.
distractor_rationale.C:
The compromised workstation can still communicate with other devices within its own
        VLAN. Segmentation limits cross-segment movement, not all network access. The malware
        could still attack other admin workstations, exfiltrate data to an external server,
        or attempt inter-VLAN traversal through the routing device.
distractor_rationale.D:
VLAN-hopping attacks (e.g., double-tagging or switch-spoofing) are real but require
        specific misconfigurations and do not give automatic access to all VLANs. Well-configured
        segmentation does not inherently allow malware to traverse all segments.

questions.skill_name: Identify security controls and explain how they mitigate risks
questions.stem:
A company has a flat network where 400 employee workstations, a public web server, and
      an internal payroll database share the same broadcast domain. The security team's primary
      concern is a compromised employee workstation reaching the payroll database. Which
      segmentation approach best addresses this goal?

choices.text: Move all employees to a single VLAN but increase logging on the payroll database server.
Encrypt all traffic on the flat network using TLS to prevent unauthorized reading of payroll data.
Separate the web server, employee workstations, and payroll database into distinct VLANs with inter-VLAN traffic controlled by a firewall.
Apply a uniform strong password policy across all devices so a single compromised credential cannot reach the payroll database.

questions.explanation:
Placing the web server, workstations, and payroll database in separate VLANs and routing
      inter-VLAN traffic through a firewall creates distinct network-level boundaries. A
      compromised workstation in the employee VLAN cannot directly reach the payroll database
      VLAN, its traffic must pass through the firewall, where a rule denying workstation-to-
      database connections can block the attempt. The public web server is also isolated from
      both internal segments, limiting the attack surface if the public server is compromised.

distractor_rationale.A:
Consolidating all employees into one VLAN does not create a boundary between the
        workstations and the payroll database, all devices remain in the same broadcast
        domain. Increased logging may improve detection but does not prevent lateral movement.
distractor_rationale.B:
TLS encrypts data in transit, protecting it from interception. It does not prevent a
        compromised device from initiating connections to the payroll database, the device
        would simply use TLS to send malicious requests to it.
distractor_rationale.D:
Strong passwords reduce credential-based attacks but do not address the network path
        between a compromised device and the payroll database. Once a workstation is compromised
        via malware (not credential theft), password policy provides no lateral movement barrier.

questions.skill_name: Identify security controls and explain how they mitigate risks
questions.stem: Compared to a flat network, how does VLAN-based segmentation improve network security?

choices.text: It enforces 802.1X authentication on all devices, preventing unauthorized users from joining the network.
It eliminates the need for a firewall because each VLAN functions as its own security perimeter.
It automatically encrypts intra-VLAN traffic to prevent data interception within a segment.
It reduces the blast radius of a security incident by limiting which devices can directly communicate with each other.

questions.explanation:
A flat network allows any device to attempt communication with any other device in the
      same broadcast domain without crossing a security boundary. VLAN segmentation divides
      devices into logical groups where direct cross-group communication is blocked at the
      Layer 2 level. An attacker or compromised device is constrained to its own segment and
      must traverse an ACL- or firewall-enforced routing point to reach other segments. This
      reduction in the blast radius of a compromise is the core security improvement over a
      flat architecture.

distractor_rationale.A:
802.1X is a port-based network access control protocol, a separate mechanism from
        VLAN segmentation, though the two can be combined. VLAN assignment alone does not
        enforce 802.1X authentication.
distractor_rationale.B:
VLANs create internal boundaries but do not replace firewalls. In fact, firewalls
        become more important in a segmented network: they are deployed at inter-VLAN routing
        points to inspect and control traffic crossing segment boundaries.
distractor_rationale.C:
VLANs do not encrypt traffic. Devices within the same VLAN communicate in cleartext
        at Layer 2. Encryption must be applied separately at the transport or application layer.

questions.skill_name: Identify security controls and explain how they mitigate risks
questions.stem:
A security architect is comparing two network designs for a corporate campus.
      Design A uses a single flat network with a hardened perimeter firewall.
      Design B uses VLAN-based segmentation with per-segment access controls at each
      inter-VLAN routing point. The architect's primary concern is minimizing the impact
      of a compromised employee workstation being used by a malicious insider.
      Which evaluation best supports choosing Design B over Design A?

choices.text: Design B is preferred because segmentation eliminates insider threats entirely by preventing all employee-to-server traffic.
Design A is preferred because a properly configured perimeter firewall is sufficient to contain threats originating from inside the network.

Design B is preferred because VLAN segmentation forces intra-campus lateral movement through access-controlled routing points, reducing the set of resources reachable from any single compromised device.
Design A is preferred because VLAN segmentation increases administrative complexity without providing measurable security benefit beyond a perimeter firewall.

questions.explanation:
A perimeter firewall (Design A) is designed to filter traffic entering and leaving the
      network boundary. It provides little or no control over lateral movement within the flat
      internal network, once an insider has network access, they can attempt connections to
      any internal resource. Design B forces all cross-segment traffic through routing points
      where ACLs can whitelist only legitimate inter-segment flows. NIST SP 800-125B and the
      broader defense-in-depth model explicitly recommend internal network segmentation to
      reduce lateral movement risk, perimeter controls alone are insufficient against insider
      threats or threats that have already bypassed the perimeter.

distractor_rationale.A:
No single control eliminates insider threats, this claim is categorically too strong.
        Segmentation raises the cost and detectability of lateral movement; it does not block
        all employee-to-server traffic, which would prevent legitimate operations.
distractor_rationale.B:
A perimeter firewall filters ingress and egress traffic at the network boundary but has
        no visibility into host-to-host traffic within a flat internal network. An insider
        operating on the internal LAN operates entirely behind the perimeter firewall.
distractor_rationale.D:
VLAN segmentation does add administrative overhead, but this is weighed against a
        documented, measurable reduction in lateral movement risk. The NIST Cybersecurity
        Framework and SP 800-53 (SC-7 Boundary Protection) identify internal segmentation as
        a substantive control, not a cosmetic one.

questions.skill_name: Identify security controls and explain how they mitigate risks
questions.stem:
A network architect proposes layering zero-trust principles on top of existing VLAN
      boundaries. A colleague argues that VLANs already provide adequate segmentation and
      zero trust adds unnecessary complexity. Which response most accurately evaluates
      this disagreement?

choices.text: The colleague is correct: VLANs fully enforce zero trust because devices in different VLANs cannot communicate by default.
The architect is correct because VLANs create coarse-grained perimeters, zero trust adds per-session identity and authorization verification that VLAN boundaries alone cannot enforce.
The architect is correct because zero trust eliminates the need for VLANs, making network segmentation redundant.
Both are incorrect: zero trust is an application-layer security model and does not interact with network-layer segmentation.

questions.explanation:
VLANs create macro-segmentation: broad zones in which all devices can freely communicate
      with each other without further challenge. Zero trust applies the principle of "never
      trust, always verify" at a finer level, every individual connection request, even
      between devices in the same VLAN, must be authenticated and authorized against a policy
      engine before it is permitted. NIST SP 800-207 (Zero Trust Architecture) explicitly
      frames VLANs as a legacy segmentation mechanism that zero trust supplements, not
      replaces. The two controls are complementary: VLANs establish network-level zones;
      zero trust enforces identity-based micro-segmentation within and across those zones.

distractor_rationale.A:
VLANs block inter-VLAN traffic by default, but all devices within a VLAN can
        communicate freely with each other. Zero trust requires per-session verification
        even within a zone, a property VLANs do not provide.
distractor_rationale.C:
Zero trust is a security model, not a physical or logical network topology replacement.
        Network segmentation (including VLANs) remains a relevant and recommended control
        within a zero trust architecture, NIST SP 800-207 describes how they coexist.
distractor_rationale.D:
Zero trust is a cross-layer model. While it encompasses application-layer authorization,
        it also directly addresses network-layer access decisions, device health verification,
        and micro-segmentation, all of which interact with network segmentation policy.

questions.skill_name: Identify security controls and explain how they mitigate risks
questions.stem:
A naval submarine network technician manages three LANs: one for weapons systems,
      one for official naval operations, and one for crew recreation. The technician must
      recommend segmentation controls proportional to each LAN's sensitivity level.
      Which design is most defensible from a security standpoint?

choices.text: Merge the weapons and operations LANs into one high-security VLAN and isolate only the recreation LAN, reducing administrative complexity while consolidating the most sensitive systems.
Connect all three LANs to a central switch without routing restrictions but install an intrusion detection sensor on the weapons LAN only.

Maintain three fully isolated segments: air-gap or hardware-firewall the weapons LAN from all other traffic, enforce strict access controls between operations and recreation, and treat recreation traffic as untrusted.
Allow the operations LAN to communicate freely with both the weapons and recreation LANs, since all crew members accessing those LANs hold appropriate clearances.

questions.explanation:
The weapons LAN controls safety-critical, potentially lethal systems. Even a single
      unauthorized command issued from another network segment, whether from a compromised
      operations workstation or a crew member's recreation device, could have catastrophic
      consequences. An air gap or hardware-enforced firewall boundary provides the strongest
      isolation and cannot be bypassed by software misconfiguration. The recreation LAN must
      be treated as the lowest-trust segment because crew members use it for personal internet
      access, maximizing its exposure to malware and social engineering. Merging the weapons
      and operations LANs (Option A) removes a critical boundary between systems of different
      sensitivity. Option D conflates personnel clearance with technical access entitlement, a violation of the principle of least privilege that zero trust frameworks (NIST SP 800-207)
      and classical defense-in-depth models both reject.

distractor_rationale.A:
Merging weapons and operations LANs eliminates the boundary between them. A compromise
        on an operations workstation, via phishing, unpatched software, or a malicious
        attachment, would then have direct network access to weapons systems, which is
        operationally and strategically unacceptable.
distractor_rationale.B:
Connecting all three LANs to a central switch without routing restrictions creates a
        flat network; no segmentation exists. IDS sensors detect attacks in progress but do
        not prevent cross-LAN lateral movement. This design provides detection without
        containment, the weakest possible architecture for this threat environment.
distractor_rationale.D:
Personnel clearance is an administrative and physical access control. It does not
        establish technical network boundaries. An authorized person's device can still be
        compromised; technical segmentation enforces access regardless of who (or what malware)
        is using the device.

questions.stem:
A hotel wants every guest room to reach the internet but no room to reach the device in
      the room next door, without giving each room its own subnet. Which segmentation technique
      fits?

choices.text: Creating a separate VLAN and routed subnet for every room
A private VLAN in which each room is an isolated port and only the uplink to the gateway is promiscuous
An air gap between the guest network and the internet
Configuring every room's switch port as an 802.1Q trunk

questions.explanation:
Private VLANs split one VLAN into a primary and secondary domains. Isolated ports can reach
      the promiscuous port (the gateway uplink) but not each other, so every room gets internet
      access while room-to-room traffic is blocked, all inside a single subnet. The hotel or
      dormitory network is the textbook use of this technique (RFC 5517).

distractor_rationale.A:
A VLAN and subnet per room would work but spends hundreds of subnets and routing
        interfaces, which is exactly what the hotel wants to avoid; private VLANs reach the same
        isolation inside one subnet.
distractor_rationale.C:
An air gap removes the network connection entirely, so guests would have no internet
        access at all.
distractor_rationale.D:
Trunk ports carry tagged traffic for many VLANs and belong between switches, not on
        guest-facing ports; a trunk on an access port is a VLAN-hopping risk, not a containment
        control.

questions.stem:
Which segmentation technique is enforced on each individual workload by policy, rather
      than at the switch (Layer 2) or the router (Layer 3)?

choices.text: A VLAN
A routed subnet with an access control list on the router
A physical air gap
Zero Trust micro-segmentation, where each workload has its own allow-list enforced by a policy enforcement point

questions.explanation:
Under Zero Trust (NIST SP 800-207), micro-segmentation gives every workload, down to a
      single virtual machine or container, an explicit list of permitted partners. A policy
      enforcement point applies it on instructions from a central policy decision point,
      regardless of IP address or VLAN membership. VLANs work at Layer 2, routed subnets and
      ACLs at Layer 3, and air gaps at the physical layer.

distractor_rationale.A: A VLAN is enforced by the switch at Layer 2, using port membership and 802.1Q tags.
distractor_rationale.B:
A routed subnet with an ACL is enforced at Layer 3 (and Layer 4 for ports) by the
        router or Layer 3 switch.
distractor_rationale.C: An air gap is enforced physically: there is no connection to cross.

questions.stem:
A company splits its network into finance, staff and guest VLANs with default-deny rules
      between them. Which threat does this segmentation do the LEAST to stop?

choices.text: Malware spreading from one finance workstation to another finance workstation on the same VLAN
A guest laptop trying to reach the finance database
A compromised staff PC scanning the finance subnet
A guest device trying to open the staff file server

questions.explanation:
A VLAN boundary only controls traffic that crosses it. Devices inside one VLAN can still
      reach each other directly at Layer 2, so a worm moving between two finance workstations
      never meets a rule. Containing that needs a finer layer, such as private VLANs, host
      firewalls or micro-segmentation. The other three all cross a zone boundary and are denied
      by default.

distractor_rationale.B:
Guest-to-finance traffic must cross the inter-VLAN boundary, where the default-deny rule
        blocks it.
distractor_rationale.C:
A scan from the staff VLAN into the finance subnet is cross-segment traffic and is
        denied at the routing point.
distractor_rationale.D:
Guest-to-staff traffic is also cross-segment and blocked by default; isolating guests
        from internal zones is the most common reason to segment.

questions.stem:
A small device plugged into an office wall port sends Dynamic Trunking Protocol frames,
      and the switch port turns into a trunk that carries every VLAN. Which switch settings
      would have prevented this, and also the related double-tagging attack?

choices.text: Enable spanning-tree portfast on every port and keep VLAN 1 as the native VLAN
Encrypt every trunk link with TLS
Set user-facing ports to access mode with switchport nonegotiate, and move each trunk's native VLAN off VLAN 1 to an unused VLAN that carries no hosts
Put every host on the native VLAN so that no frames need tags

questions.explanation:
Switch spoofing works because the port is left negotiating; fixing it in access mode with
      DTP disabled (switchport nonegotiate) means it can never become a trunk. Double tagging
      relies on the trunk carrying its native VLAN untagged; moving the native VLAN to an unused
      ID with no hosts on it removes the attacker's starting point. Together these are the two
      rules almost every VLAN-hopping checklist comes down to.

distractor_rationale.A:
Portfast only speeds up how quickly a port starts forwarding; leaving VLAN 1 as the
        native VLAN is the exact condition double tagging needs.
distractor_rationale.B:
TLS protects application data between two endpoints; it does not stop a switch port from
        negotiating into a trunk or a switch from forwarding a double-tagged frame.
distractor_rationale.D:
Putting hosts on the native VLAN is what makes double tagging possible; the native VLAN
        should carry no host traffic at all.

questions.stem:
In the 2013 Target breach, attackers used an HVAC contractor's stolen credentials to log
      in to a vendor billing portal, then moved through the internal network to the
      point-of-sale registers. Which control would most directly have contained the stolen
      credentials?

choices.text: Stronger antivirus on the point-of-sale registers only
Placing the vendor portal in its own zone with default-deny rules between it and the cardholder data environment
A larger, faster perimeter firewall at the internet edge
Encrypting the card database at rest

questions.explanation:
The Senate investigation found the vendor portal was not adequately separated from the
      internal network, so a credential theft anywhere became a credential theft everywhere.
      Isolating third-party access in its own segment, with default-deny rules to the
      cardholder data environment as PCI-DSS segmentation guidance describes, would have
      confined the attackers to a low-value zone. That is blast-radius reduction.

distractor_rationale.A:
Endpoint protection on the registers is a useful extra layer, but it does nothing to stop
        the attacker reaching them, and it leaves every other internal system as exposed as
        before.
distractor_rationale.C:
The attackers came in through a legitimate, permitted vendor login; a bigger perimeter
        firewall allows the same login and has no say over traffic once inside.
distractor_rationale.D:
The malware read card data from register memory before it was encrypted, so encryption at
        rest in a database would not have protected it.

questions.stem:
A public web server must be reachable from the internet, but if it is compromised it must
      not be able to reach internal file shares or the domain controllers. Which design meets
      both requirements?

choices.text: Put the web server on the staff VLAN and rely on its host firewall
Keep a flat internal network and put the web server behind the same perimeter firewall as everything else
Air-gap the web server from every other network
Place the web server in a DMZ separated from the internal network by a further firewall boundary, with no shared credentials or direct trust between DMZ hosts and the internal domain

questions.explanation:
A DMZ, built with two firewalls or one firewall with three interfaces, lets the internet
      reach the public service while adding at least one more boundary before anything internal.
      Because DMZ hosts hold no shared credentials or open database access into the internal
      domain, a compromised web server has no direct path to file shares or domain controllers.

distractor_rationale.A:
On the staff VLAN the server sits beside internal workstations; one compromise of an
        internet-facing service lands the attacker inside the staff zone.
distractor_rationale.B:
Behind a single perimeter on a flat network, the compromised server can reach every
        internal host directly; this is the castle-and-moat weakness segmentation exists to fix.
distractor_rationale.C:
An air gap would make the server unreachable from the internet, which defeats its
        purpose.

questions.stem:
In May 2021, Colonial Pipeline shut down its entire pipeline for about six days, even
      though investigators found no evidence the ransomware reached the operational technology
      (OT) that runs the pumps and valves. Which explanation, and which set of layered controls,
      best fits the lesson of the case?

choices.text: The ransomware had encrypted the pipeline's controllers; antivirus on the controllers would have kept it running
The company had no firewall at all; adding a perimeter firewall would have kept it running

The company could not verify during the incident that its IT/OT boundary had held; a documented Purdue-style boundary with an OT DMZ (no direct IT-to-OT traffic), continuous monitoring of that boundary, and MFA on remote access would have closed the entry point and let it show OT was isolated
The company shut down only to speed up ransom negotiations; paying sooner would have avoided the shutdown

questions.explanation:
The entry point was a legacy VPN account with a leaked password and no MFA. The shutdown
      happened because the company could not prove fast enough that the infection, or corrupted
      data from billing systems, could not affect safe pipeline operation. A boundary that exists
      only on a diagram cannot be relied on in an incident. The layered answer names three
      controls that fail independently: MFA on remote access, a Purdue-model IT/OT boundary with
      an OT DMZ, and monitoring that proves the boundary is holding.

distractor_rationale.A:
Investigators found no evidence that the OT systems were breached; the shutdown was
        precautionary.
distractor_rationale.B:
The problem was a single unprotected remote-access account and an IT/OT boundary nobody
        could vouch for, not the absence of a perimeter firewall; a perimeter firewall still lets
        a valid VPN login through.
distractor_rationale.D:
Paying does not make a doubtful boundary trustworthy; the shutdown came from uncertainty
        about OT safety, which a ransom payment does not resolve.

questions.stem:
In a data centre, two web servers share one VLAN and subnet. They should reach the
      application tier only on TCP 8443 and have no reason to talk to each other. The architect
      wants layers that fail independently. Which design is best?

choices.text: Keep the VLAN and subnet boundary between tiers with default-deny ACLs, add per-workload micro-segmentation allowing only web-to-app on 8443 and no web-to-web traffic, and monitor east-west traffic for unexpected connections
Collapse all tiers into one VLAN and rely on Zero Trust policy alone, since it makes network boundaries unnecessary
Replace the inter-tier ACLs with a private VLAN, since isolated ports already enforce port-level rules between tiers
Rely on antivirus on each server to stop lateral movement

questions.explanation:
Coarse VLAN and ACL boundaries contain whole tiers; micro-segmentation adds a fine-grained
      allow-list on each workload that also blocks the web-to-web path a shared VLAN would leave
      open; east-west monitoring (for example network detection and response sensors) catches what
      slips past both. Each layer would fail for a different reason, which is what defence in
      depth requires. NIST SP 800-207 treats VLAN segmentation and Zero Trust as complementary.

distractor_rationale.B:
Zero Trust supplements network segmentation rather than replacing it; removing the coarse
        boundary throws away an independent layer.
distractor_rationale.C:
A private VLAN controls which ports can talk at Layer 2 within one VLAN; it cannot express
        a rule such as "web to app on TCP 8443 only" between tiers.
distractor_rationale.D:
Antivirus is an endpoint control that reacts after a threat lands; it creates no boundary
        and does not restrict which hosts can connect to which.

questions.stem:
A DMZ uses private VLANs, with each server on an isolated port. During a penetration test,
      a tester on one compromised DMZ server still manages to send traffic to another DMZ server.
      Which explanation and response are most accurate?

choices.text: Private VLANs encrypt traffic between ports, so the tester must have stolen the encryption key; rotate the key
Isolated ports are meant to talk to each other; move the servers to community ports to stop it
Private VLANs only work on wireless networks; move the DMZ to Wi-Fi

Private VLANs are a containment control, not an authentication one, and a host that forges Layer 2 frames or bounces traffic through the gateway can get around them; add port security on the switch, default-deny rules at the gateway, and host-level allow-lists on each server

questions.explanation:
Private VLANs stop isolated ports talking directly, but a device that ignores the subnet and
      forges frames, or sends traffic to the gateway for routing back into the same subnet, can
      get around them unless other controls are present. The layered response is port security
      on the switch, default-deny rules on the gateway so it will not route DMZ-to-DMZ traffic,
      and per-server allow-lists so each host refuses connections it has no reason to accept.

distractor_rationale.A: Private VLANs do not encrypt anything; they restrict which ports may exchange frames.
distractor_rationale.B:
Isolated ports cannot reach each other by design, and community ports would make things
        worse, because community members can talk freely among themselves.
distractor_rationale.C:
Private VLANs are an Ethernet switch feature (RFC 5517) and are commonly used on wired
        DMZ switches; moving servers to Wi-Fi would only widen the attack surface.
